scope: Follow-up to the six low-confidence rows in data/dmv_test_languages.json. Primary agency pages were read; no confidence was inflated merely because a page was reachable.
app_decision: All six shipping state configs lack official_test_languages evidence, so the iOS app conservatively labels their non-English banks as study aids and offers English practice. This review does not alter those configs or declare unknown languages unavailable.

results.finding: The current page requires an in-person knowledge exam but does not enumerate its available languages.
results.limit: A missing language list is not proof of English-only testing. The older third-party EN/ES claim remains unconfirmed.

results.source: Montana MVD forms and driver manuals
results.finding: The agency lists Spanish, Arabic, Dari and Swahili study manuals.
results.limit: Manual translations do not establish the language menu for the actual knowledge exam; do not promote the 2016 test-language list to current verified fact.

results.finding: The online-exam FAQ expressly says its written test is available only in English.
results.quote: At this time, the written test is only available in English.
results.limit: This is an online-test statement. It does not resolve all in-person or CareerTech testing options.

results.finding: The current page explains branch and authorized third-party testing but does not enumerate exam languages.
results.limit: The legacy four-language list is not re-verified by this page.

results.source: South Dakota agency highway-safety planning document
results.finding: An agency planning document records that the written driver-license exam became available in Spanish in 2020.
results.quote: In 2020, the written portion of the driver license exam was made available in Spanish.
results.limit: This provides primary historical support for Spanish, not a complete current exam-language menu. Current application/manual translations alone are insufficient evidence.

results.finding: The current official page links knowledge-testing resources and an interpreter/translator form.
results.limit: It does not enumerate a complete current exam-language menu. An interpreter form or translated registration page does not prove a particular exam is offered in that language.

remaining: Verify the actual non-commercial testing modes/languages with the relevant agencies before claiming full resolution of #58. Keep old evidence and separate online, in-person, interpreter and translated-handbook facts.
